$comment: Contract 18 §7-AI S1 — the DOCUMENT-settings typed ALLOWLIST (kills AF1). A page/document settings bag is open (unknown keys pass through verbatim), but the known keys below are validated for render-fatal shapes: page-settings `custom_css` MUST be a plain string — the object `{raw:<base64>}` shape is the STYLE-VARIANT form (contract 11 §5) and on PAGE settings it fatals Elementor Pro's custom-css module (`trim()` on an array, elementor-pro/modules/custom-css/module.php:101) for every visitor. This is the AF1 inverse-trap pair: style custom_css REQUIRES the object; page-settings custom_css REQUIRES the string. Violations map to taxonomy code SETTINGS_INVALID (12-error-taxonomy.md §3.1). The PHP validator (Validator::validate_settings) is AUTHORITATIVE; the TS pageSettingsInputSchema mirrors this allowlist as a prefilter only. Source of truth: this file; packages/shared/schemas/page-settings.schema.json is the CI-checked byte-identical mirror (scripts/sync-schemas.mjs).

custom_css.$comment: Plain CSS string (NOT base64, NOT the {raw} object). REJECT object/array → SETTINGS_INVALID.

template.$comment: The `_wp_page_template` page template (incl. elementor_canvas per §7-AI S1).

hide_title.$comment: Boolean per §7-AI S1; the legacy Elementor switcher strings 'yes'/'' are also accepted so stored settings round-trip.
